title: China Is Building a Global Infrastructure for Its Cultural Industries
author: Leonie Spangenberg
text:
Credit: Depositphotos
On September 4, Lingang New Area in Shanghai launched an AI+micro-drama overseas service station, with initial service points in Saudi Arabia, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland. The initiative is designed to help Chinese companies navigate overseas regulations, localize content, and connect production with distribution in foreign markets. The service station covers the full export chain including content development, production, translation, and distribution. Rather than simply helping companies sell finished dramas abroad, it brings several stages of the export process into one system. Online literature, games, and micro-dramas are increasingly described in China as the “New Three” of cultural exports. All three can be adapted, translated, and distributed through digital platforms, making the process of taking them overseas simpler.[...]
